mainTopic: צאן ברזל from a נכרי and the בכורה exemption: whose רשות the flock is in, יד גוי באמצע, and how many generations are exempt (רב הונא vs. רב יהודה)
overview: This עמוד finishes the משנה about a Jew who takes צאן ברזל (a 'guaranteed investment' flock) from a נכרי. The direct offspring are exempt from בכורה. If the Jew set the offspring in place of their mothers as security, the grandchildren are exempt too. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says even ten generations are exempt. The משנה then rules on a רחל that gives birth to a goat-like animal: it is exempt unless the newborn has some of its mother's features. The גמרא asks whether our משנה shows that צאן ברזל stays in the owner's רשות, and it contrasts this with the רבית law, which treats the flock as the receiver's. אביי answers that the two משניות describe different deals. רבא rejects that answer and says the flock belongs to the receiver in both; the exemption comes from יד גוי באמצע, because the נכרי can seize the animal or its offspring. Next, רב הונא and רב יהודה argue about how many generations are exempt when no offspring were set as security. The גמרא defends רב יהודה from the משנה's wording, then begins a challenge to רב הונא from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's word 'אפילו', which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Offspring of the flock are exempt; grandchildren are obligated
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the direct offspring of צאן ברזל taken from a נכרי are exempt from בכורה, but the offspring of those offspring are obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their offspring are exempt, but the offspring of their offspring are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its case of a Jew who received צאן ברזל from a נכרי. It tells us which generations of animals are exempt from the law of בכורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נכרי has a claim on the flock. If the fixed payment is not made, he can collect from the mothers and from their direct offspring. Because the נכרי has a hold on the first generation (יד גוי באמצע), those animals are exempt from בכורה. The next generation is beyond his claim, so it is obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Iron sheep': an investment where the receiver guarantees the full value to the owner no matter what happens
The law of the firstborn male animal

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'their offspring' refer to the צאן ברזל from the end of the previous section of the משנה: a Jew who took the flock from a נכרי. This is not a new case.

phrases.english: their offspring are exempt,
phrases.notes: Referring to the צאן ברזל received from a gentile

phrases.english: the offspring of their offspring are obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous daf about צאן ברזל from a נכרי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First-generation offspring of צאן ברזל from a נכרי are exempt from בכורה; the second generation is obligated.

steps.title: When offspring are pledged in place of their mothers
steps.stepSummary: If the Jew set up the offspring as security in place of the mothers, the exemption moves down one generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he set their offspring in place of their mothers, then the offspring of the offspring are exempt, and the offspring of the offspring of the offspring are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a variation. The Jew made the offspring the security for the נכרי instead of the mothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the offspring take over the mothers' role as security, the נכרי's claim now also covers their own offspring. So the exemption extends one generation further than before. Only the generation after that is free of his claim and obligated in בכורה.

phrases.english: If he established their offspring in place of their mothers,
phrases.notes: As the guarantee for the gentile

phrases.english: the offspring of the offspring are exempt,
and the offspring of the offspring of the offspring are obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule of step 1 to the case where the offspring replace the mothers as security.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the offspring replace the mothers as security, the exemption extends one more generation.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: even ten generations are exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that every later generation stays exempt, because the guarantee to the נכרי covers them all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Even up to ten generations they are exempt, because they serve as a guarantee for the נכרי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with the ruling just stated. He holds that the exemption does not stop after one or two generations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, the נכרי's right to collect reaches every descendant of the flock. If the fixed payment is not made, he can take any of them. So the נכרי has a stake in all of them, and none is subject to בכורה.
steps.whatToRemember: The more far-reaching the נכרי's claim on the animals, the further the בכורה exemption extends. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds the claim reaches all generations.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
even up to ten generations are exempt,
since they serve as a guarantee for the gentile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the generational limit set in steps 1 and 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All generations of the flock are exempt, since all are subject to the נכרי's claim.

steps.title: A ewe that gives birth to a goat-like animal
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that a ewe that gives birth to something like a goat, or a goat that gives birth to something like a ewe, is exempt from בכורה, unless the newborn has some of its mother's features.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ewe that gave birth to a goat-like animal, or a goat that gave birth to a ewe-like animal, is exempt from בכורה. If the newborn has some of the signs (of its mother), it is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new topic. Now the question is not who owns the animal but whether the newborn looks like its mother's species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור must be of the same kind as its mother. If a ewe bears something that looks like a goat, the newborn is not treated as its mother's 'firstborn' for this law. If the newborn has even some of its mother's features, it counts and is obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind or species; here, 'something like'

phrases.english: A ewe that gave birth to a goat of sorts,
and a goat that gave birth to a ewe of sorts,
is exempt from the law of the firstborn,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין — חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: and if it has some of the characteristics (of its mother), it is obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה topic, unrelated to the צאן ברזל discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A newborn that does not resemble its mother's species is exempt from בכורה, unless it has some of the mother's features.

steps.title: Is צאן ברזל still in the owner's possession?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws an inference from the משנה: since the owner has not yet taken his money, the flock seems to remain in the owner's רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Is this to say that since the owner has not taken his money, the flock stands in the owner's possession?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first case of the משנה, צאן ברזל. It asks what that ruling implies about ownership. This is setting up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offspring were exempt because the נכרי has a share in them. That suggests the נכרי, the original owner, still owns the flock until he is paid. The גמרא states this inference so it can test it against another source.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? (draws an inference)

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: לְמֵימְרָא, דְּכֵיוָן דְּלָא נָקֵט מָרָא זוּזֵי —
phrases.english: Is this to say that since the owner did not take the money,
it stands in the owner's possession?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא, דְּכֵיוָן דְּלָא נָקֵט מָרָא זוּזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the צאן ברזל ruling of step 1 and draws an inference about ownership.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה implies that צאן ברזל remains in the original owner's רשות until he is paid.

steps.title: Contradiction from the רבית law: the flock belongs to the receiver
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference with a משנה that forbids taking צאן ברזל from a Jew because it is רבית. That implies the flock belongs to the receiver.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contradicted it: One may not accept צאן ברזל from a Jew, because it is רבית. Evidently, it stands in the possession of the receiver!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from מסכת בבא מציעא that seems to contradict the inference in step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A deal can only count as רבית if it is a loan. A loan means the item now belongs to the borrower, here the receiver. So that משנה treats צאן ברזל as the receiver's property, which is the opposite of what our משנה implied.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it (introduces a contradiction between sources)

steps.confusionAlert: The רבית problem only arises if the receiver owns the flock, making it a loan. That is exactly why this משנה clashes with the idea that the original owner still owns it.

phrases.aramaic: וּרְמִינְהוּ: אֵין מְקַבְּלִין צֹאן בַּרְזֶל מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction: One may not accept a guaranteed-investment flock from a Jew
because it is interest,
evidently it stands in the possession of the recipient!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference made in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that צאן ברזל remains in the owner's רשות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבית prohibition only applies to a loan, so it assumes the receiver owns the flock. That contradicts the inference that the owner still owns it.

steps.title: אביי: the two cases involve different deals
steps.stepSummary: אביי says there is no contradiction. Our משנה is a case where the owner accepted the risk of accidents and price drops. The משנה in בבא מציעא is a case where he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is not difficult. This case is where he accepted upon himself loss from accidents and from price drops. That case is where he did not accept upon himself loss from accidents and price drops.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction from Step 6. He says the two משניות are talking about two different kinds of deals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner takes the risk of loss (אונסא וזולא), the animals are still really his. That is why our משנה treats them as being in the נכרי's רשות and exempts them from בכורה. If the owner takes no risk, the flock belongs to the receiver, and making the receiver pay a guaranteed return is רבית.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Loss from an accident, such as the animal dying
Loss from a drop in market value

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult.
This is where he accepted upon himself loss from accidents and price drops,
phrases.notes: Our משנה: the owner bears the risk, so the animals stay his.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא דְּלָא קַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ אוּנְסָא וְזוֹלָא.
phrases.english: and that is where he did not accept upon himself loss from accidents and price drops.
phrases.notes: The משנה in בבא מציעא: no risk for the owner, so the flock belongs to the receiver.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each משנה describes a different arrangement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות describe the same צאן ברזל deal, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is a deal where the owner takes the risk. The other משנה is a deal where he does not.

steps.title: רבא: a deal with risk to the owner is not צאן ברזל
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects to אביי. If the owner takes on the risk of loss, the deal cannot be called צאן ברזל. Also, both משניות use the term without any qualification.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If he accepted upon himself loss from accidents and price drops, do you call that 'iron sheep'? And furthermore, why is it stated without qualification?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts attacking אביי's answer. This step gives his first two objections.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name צאן ברזל means 'iron flock': for the owner, the value can never be lost. A deal where the owner takes the risk is the opposite of that, so it cannot carry this name. Also, if the term covered two different deals, the משניות should have said which one they meant, but both state it plainly.

keyTerms.meaning: Why is it stated without qualification, as a blanket statement?

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
If he accepted upon himself loss from accidents and price drops,
do you call that 'iron sheep'?
phrases.notes: 'Iron' means the owner's value never gets lost. Here it can be lost.

phrases.english: And furthermore, why is it stated without qualification?

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's reading of our משנה as a deal where the owner bears the risk
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Such a deal does not fit the definition of צאן ברזל. Also, the משניות use the term with no qualification.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה should have made the distinction inside the Jewish case
steps.stepSummary: רבא's third objection: if אביי were right, the משנה in בבא מציעא should have permitted a risk-bearing deal even with a Jew. It should not have needed to switch to the case of a נכרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, instead of teaching in the last clause 'But one may accept iron sheep from a gentile,' let it make a distinction within its own case and teach: When is this said? When he did not accept upon himself loss from accidents and price drops. But if he accepted upon himself loss from accidents and price drops, it is perfectly fine!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a third objection to אביי. He argues from how the משנה in בבא מציעא is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That משנה ends by allowing צאן ברזל from a נכרי. If a deal where the owner takes the risk were also called צאן ברזל and were permitted, the משנה should have stated that simpler permitted case right within the Jewish case. Since it did not, it seems צאן ברזל always means a deal with no risk to the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of a משנה
Let it make a distinction and teach within the same case
When is this statement said? (limits a ruling)

phrases.english: And furthermore, instead of teaching in the last clause

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְקַבְּלִין צֹאן בַּרְזֶל מִן הַגּוֹי —
phrases.english: 'But one may accept iron sheep from a gentile,'
let it make a distinction and teach within its own case:
When is this said?
When he did not accept upon himself loss from accidents and price drops,
but if he accepted upon himself loss from accidents and price drops,
it is perfectly fine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third objection to אביי, continuing Step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's claim that צאן ברזל can include a deal where the owner takes the risk
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה in בבא מציעא would have taught this permitted case directly. It does not.

steps.title: רבא's answer: the נכרי can seize the animals
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both משניות describe the same deal, where the owner takes no risk, and the flock belongs to the receiver. The exemption from בכורה comes from a different reason: the נכרי can seize the animal or its offspring if he is not paid, so there is יד גוי באמצע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Both this case and that case are where he did not accept upon himself loss from accidents and price drops. And here, regarding the firstborn, this is the reason: if the gentile comes and wants his money and the Jew does not give it to him, he seizes the animal. If he does not find the animal, he seizes its offspring. So the gentile's hand is in the middle, and wherever the gentile's hand is in the middle, the animal is exempt from the firstborn law.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops אביי's approach and gives his own answer to the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no contradiction about ownership: in both משניות the flock belongs to the Jewish receiver. The exemption from בכורה does not come from the נכרי owning the animals. It comes from his right to seize the animal or its offspring as payment. That partial hold (יד גוי באמצע) is enough to exempt the animal from בכורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that; both cases
A non-Jew's hand is in the middle; the non-Jew has a partial hold on the animal
Exempt from the laws of the firstborn

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, צאן ברזל belongs to the receiver. That is why taking it from a Jew is רבית. Yet the animals are exempt from בכורה because the נכרי's right to seize them creates יד גוי באמצע.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is saying the נכרי owns the animals. He agrees they belong to the Jew. The exemption comes only from the נכרי's right to seize them for payment.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer sets a key principle: even a partial claim by a non-Jew, such as a right to seize the animal for a debt, is enough to exempt an animal from בכורה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי דְּלָא קַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ אוּנְסָא וְזוֹלָא,
phrases.english: Both this and that are where he did not accept upon himself loss from accidents and price drops,
and here, regarding the firstborn, this is the reason:
if the gentile comes and wants his money
and the Jew does not give it to him,
he seizes the animal,
and if he does not find the animal,
he seizes its offspring.
So the gentile's hand is in the middle,
and wherever the gentile's hand is in the middle,
the animal is exempt from the firstborn law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting אביי in Steps 8 and 9, רבא gives a new answer to the contradiction from Step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the reason: the exemption is based on the נכרי's right to seize the animals, not on his ownership
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה exempts the animals because they still belong to the נכרי, which contradicts the רבית ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The flock belongs to the receiver in both משניות. The exemption comes from יד גוי באמצע, because the נכרי can seize the animal or its offspring.

steps.title: The משנה's case: offspring set in place of their mothers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה: if the Jew set the offspring in place of their mothers, the grandchildren are also exempt from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he set their offspring in place of their mothers, the offspring of the offspring are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from our משנה so it can discuss it. This is a setup for the dispute in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a צאן ברזל deal with a נכרי, the Jew owes the נכרי the value of the animals. Here the Jew agreed that if a mother animal dies, its offspring will take its place as the נכרי's security. Because the נכרי has a claim on those offspring, even the grandchildren are exempt from בכורה.

keyTerms.meaning: He set up / established (here: set the offspring in place of the mothers as security)
Offspring of offspring (the second generation, the grandchildren)
Exempt (here: from the laws of בכורה)

phrases.english: If he set their offspring in place of their mothers —
phrases.notes: The offspring become the נכרי's security in case the mothers die.

phrases.english: the offspring of the offspring are exempt.
phrases.notes: Exempt from בכורה because of the נכרי's claim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the general discussion of צאן ברזל to the next clause of the משנה about the offspring.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the offspring were set in place of the mothers, the grandchildren are exempt from בכורה.

steps.title: How many generations are exempt when nothing was set aside
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says only the first generation is exempt. רב יהודה says the second generation is exempt too, and only the third generation is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The offspring are exempt, but the offspring of the offspring are obligated. רב יהודה said: The offspring of the offspring are also exempt, and only the offspring of the offspring of the offspring are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים argue about how far down the family line the exemption from בכורה reaches. This is in a case where the Jew did not set the offspring in place of the mothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without such an agreement, only the mother animals are clearly the נכרי's security. רב הונא holds that the נכרי's claim reaches only her direct offspring. רב יהודה holds that it reaches one generation further, to the grandchildren.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא: only the first generation is exempt
An אמורא: the first two generations are exempt

steps.confusionAlert: The dispute is about a case where he did NOT set the offspring in place of their mothers. The משנה's case, where he did set them, is the one quoted in the step before.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The offspring are exempt,
but the offspring of the offspring are obligated.
phrases.notes: The bracketed word is the corrected reading.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said:
The offspring of the offspring are also exempt,
and the offspring of the offspring of the offspring are obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a dispute about the case next to the one in the משנה, where the offspring were not set as security.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: one generation is exempt. רב יהודה: two generations are exempt.

steps.title: The משנה's wording seems to refute רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה exempts the grandchildren only when he set the offspring in place of their mothers. That implies that without it, the grandchildren are obligated, which goes against רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: If he set the offspring in place of their mothers, the offspring of the offspring are exempt. The reason is that he set them. But if he did not set them, they are not exempt. This is a refutation of רב יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes an inference from the משנה's wording and uses it to attack רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ties the exemption of the grandchildren to the fact that he set the offspring in place of their mothers. So if he did not, the grandchildren should be obligated, exactly as רב הונא says. רב יהודה says they are exempt even then, so the משנה seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is…, used to draw an inference from a condition
But (if not)…, introducing the opposite case

phrases.english: We learned:
If he set the offspring in place of their mothers —
the offspring of the offspring are exempt.
The reason is that he set them,
but if he did not set them — they are not exempt.
This is a refutation of Rav Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה from step 11 to challenge רב יהודה's view from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's view that the grandchildren are exempt even when the offspring were not set as security.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's condition (he set them) implies the opposite result when the condition is missing: the grandchildren would be obligated.

steps.title: רב יהודה rejects the inference
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the grandchildren are exempt even when he did not set the offspring as security. The משנה chose this case to teach something new: even when he did set them, the exemption stops at the same point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה could say to you: The same is true even if he did not set them. And the משנה is teaching us this: even if he did set them, the rule is the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יהודה. It says the משנה's condition is not meant to exclude the case where he did not set the offspring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference in step 13 assumed that the case of setting the offspring gives more exemption than not setting them. רב יהודה says it does not. The משנה mentions setting them to show that even then, the exemption reaches only the grandchildren and not every later generation.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you, introducing a defense
It teaches us (the new point of the text)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין, אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא הֶעֱמִיד,
phrases.english: The same is true even though he did not set them,
and this is what it teaches us:
even if he set them, it is the same.
phrases.notes: Even then, only two generations are exempt, not more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 by changing what the משנה's condition is meant to teach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the משנה's חידוש: the condition does not exclude the other case. It teaches a new point about the case it mentions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Setting the offspring as security is what exempts the grandchildren, so without it they are obligated.
steps.terutzMaskana: Grandchildren are exempt either way. The משנה teaches that setting the offspring does not stretch the exemption past the grandchildren.

steps.title: Why setting the offspring adds nothing
steps.stepSummary: The נכרי normally seizes the young anyway, so setting the offspring in place of their mothers changes nothing. The case is treated like one where he did not set them: the grandchildren are exempt and the great-grandchildren are obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is the normal way of a נכרי to seize her young, so it is as if he did not set them. The offspring of the offspring are exempt, and the offspring of the offspring of the offspring are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב יהודה's answer. It explains why the משנה needed to say that setting the offspring as security does not add more exempt generations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think that once the offspring are formally set as security, the נכרי's claim continues down every generation. The גמרא says no. A נכרי grabs the young anyway, so the formal agreement adds nothing. The result is the same as with no agreement: two generations are exempt, and the third is obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: Like one who did not set them

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יהודה, the grandchildren of a צאן ברזל flock from a נכרי are exempt from בכורה whether or not the offspring were set as security. The great-grandchildren are obligated. Setting the offspring as security adds nothing, because the נכרי seizes the young anyway.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the exemption from בכורה depends on the real reach of the נכרי's claim (יד גוי). A formal agreement that does not change that reach does not change the law.

phrases.english: For it is the normal way of a gentile to seize her young,
so it is like one who did not set them —
the offspring of the offspring are exempt,
and the offspring of the offspring of the offspring are obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב יהודה's answer in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the reason: the agreement adds nothing to what the נכרי would seize anyway.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Formally setting the offspring as security would exempt every later generation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case equals not setting them: the grandchildren are exempt and the great-grandchildren are obligated.

steps.title: Quoting רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: exempt even for ten generations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the offspring are exempt from בכורה even down to ten generations, because the נכרי holds them as security.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: even until ten generations they are exempt, because they serve as a guarantee for the נכרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a line from the משנה to set up a challenge. The challenge itself starts in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל goes much further than the תנא קמא and exempts ten generations. His reason is that every later generation is also security for the נכרי, so the נכרי has a share in them. Watch his word 'אפילו' (even). The גמרא is about to build its challenge on it.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה). Used to quote a source.
Even. It hints that the other opinion also went part of the way.
Responsibility or guarantee. Here it means the animals are security for a debt.
A non-Jew. Here, the partner who gave the animals.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new argument. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is part of the same משנה. The גמרא is using his wording to test the argument between רב הונא and רב יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: We learned: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Even until ten generations they are exempt,
phrases.notes: The word 'even' is the key to the coming challenge.

phrases.english: because they serve as a guarantee for the gentile.
phrases.notes: If the נכרי is not paid, he can collect from any of the offspring.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending רב יהודה (steps 13-15) to a new source that will be used against רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: offspring are exempt from בכורה even down to ten generations, because they are security for the נכרי.

steps.title: The word 'even' fits רב יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its challenge. According to רב יהודה, the תנא קמא already exempts more than one generation, so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's word 'אפילו' makes sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works out well according to רב יהודה, who says the תנא קמא went down through the generations...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a 'בשלמא' challenge by first showing which opinion the wording fits. The sentence breaks off here and continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה holds that the תנא קמא exempts two generations, the children and the grandchildren. So the תנא קמא also counts generations, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל can say 'even ten generations', meaning 'not just two, but even ten'. The next passage will ask how 'even' makes sense for רב הונא, who exempts only the first generation.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well for... The first half of a challenge that will then hit the other side.
Went down to, or dealt with
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here thinking the גמרא proved רב יהודה right. 'בשלמא' only says the wording fits him. The real attack, on רב הונא, comes next.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge tests the argument between רב הונא and רב יהודה. It uses the wording of the משנה itself, the word 'even', as evidence for how far the תנא קמא's exemption goes.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rav Yehuda, who says:
the first tanna descended to the generations —
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the word 'אפילו' from step 16 as the basis of a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that only the first generation is exempt (the attack on him is completed on the next עמוד).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'אפילו' suggests the תנא קמא also exempted several generations. That fits רב יהודה (two generations) but seems not to fit רב הונא (only one generation).
